The leading causes of death in the United States are heart disease and cancer. However, in 2022, COVID-19 was the fourth leading cause of death in the United States, accounting for around six percent of all deaths that year. In 2022, there were around 45 deaths from COVID-19 per 100,000 population.   
  
**Cardiovascular disease**  
  
[Deaths from cardiovascular disease are more common among men](https://www.statista.com/statistics/189737/deaths-by-heart-diseases-in-the-us-by-gender-since-1950/) than women but have decreased for both sexes over the past few decades. [Coronary heart disease accounts for the highest portion of cardiovascular disease deaths](https://www.statista.com/statistics/671195/cardiovascular-disease-death-distribution-us-by-type/) in the United States, followed by stroke and high blood pressure. The [states with the highest death rates from cardiovascular disease](https://www.statista.com/statistics/320799/top-us-states-by-heart-disease-deaths/) include Oklahoma, Mississippi, and Alabama. Smoking tobacco, physical inactivity, poor diet, stress, and being overweight or obese are all risk factors for developing heart disease.   
  
**Cancer**  
  
 Although cancer is the second leading cause of death in the United States, like deaths from cardiovascular disease, deaths from cancer have decreased over the last few decades. The [highest death rates from cancer](https://www.statista.com/statistics/268492/us-death-rates-from-cancer-by-type-and-gender/) come from lung cancer for both men and women. Breast cancer is the second deadliest cancer for women, while prostate cancer is the second deadliest cancer for men. West Virginia, Mississippi, and Kentucky [lead the nation with the highest cancer death rates.](https://www.statista.com/statistics/248555/us-states-with-the-highest-cancer-death-rate/)

The leading causes of death in the United States are heart disease and cancer. However, in 2022, COVID-19 was the fourth leading cause of death in the United States, accounting for around six percent of all deaths that year. In 2022, there were around 45 deaths from COVID-19 per 100,000 population.   
  
**Cardiovascular disease**  
  
[Deaths from cardiovascular disease are more common among men](https://www.statista.com/statistics/189737/deaths-by-heart-diseases-in-the-us-by-gender-since-1950/) than women but have decreased for both sexes over the past few decades. [Coronary heart disease accounts for the highest portion of cardiovascular disease deaths](https://www.statista.com/statistics/671195/cardiovascular-disease-death-distribution-us-by-type/) in the United States, followed by stroke and high blood pressure. The [states with the highest death rates from cardiovascular disease](https://www.statista.com/statistics/320799/top-us-states-by-heart-disease-deaths/) include Oklahoma, Mississippi, and Alabama. Smoking tobacco, physical inactivity, poor diet, stress, and being overweight or obese are all risk factors for developing heart disease.   
  
**Cancer**  
  
 Although cancer is the second leading cause of death in the United States, like deaths from cardiovascular disease, deaths from cancer have decreased over the last few decades. The [highest death rates from cancer](https://www.statista.com/statistics/268492/us-death-rates-from-cancer-by-type-and-gender/) come from lung cancer for both men and women. Breast cancer is the second deadliest cancer for women, while prostate cancer is the second deadliest cancer for men. West Virginia, Mississippi, and Kentucky [lead the nation with the highest cancer death rates.](https://www.statista.com/statistics/248555/us-states-with-the-highest-cancer-death-rate/)

**Final Information**

The supplied page contains data describing the national (U.S.‑wide) distribution of causes of death for the year 2022.  It does not provide state‑specific figures for COVID‑19 mortality, suicide mortality, or a listing of whether heart disease is the leading cause of death in individual states.  The page does, however, confirm the national ranking of heart disease as the leading cause of death.

| Entity | Year | Condition / Value | Source Quote |
|--------|------|-------------------|--------------|
| Heart disease | 2022 | Leading cause of death in the U.S. (26.2 % of all deaths) | “Heart disease was the leading cause of death in the US, accounting for an average of 702,880 deaths (26.2 % of all deaths)” (Paragraph 1 of Results) |
| Malignant neoplasms | 2022 | Second leading cause of death in the U.S. (22.7 %) | “followed by malignant neoplasms (22.7 % of all deaths)” (Paragraph 1) |
| Unintentional injuries | 2022 | Third leading cause of death in the U.S. (8.5 %) | “unintentional injuries (8.5 %)” (Paragraph 1) |
| COVID‑19 | 2022 | Fourth leading cause of death in the U.S. (6.9 %) | “COVID‑19 … (6.9 %)” (Paragraph 1) |
| Heart disease | 2022 | Leading cause of death for men (26.8 %) and women (25.4 %) | “Heart disease (26.8 % of all deaths for men and 25.4 % for women)” (Paragraph 1) |

**Page**  
Full article: “Leading Causes of US Deaths in the 2022” (NIH PMC: 3940644).  The page includes the article’s abstract, introduction, materials and methods, results, discussion, references, and meta‑data.

**Evidence**  
- Paragraph 1 of the Results section (national death counts and percentages).  
- Paragraph 2 of Results (sex‑specific ranking).  
- Abstract (summary of top ten causes).  
- Table 1 referenced in the Discussion (although the table itself is not reproduced in the supplied text).

**Coverage**  
- National (U.S.‑wide) leading causes of death for 2022.  
- Percentages of deaths attributed to heart disease, malignant neoplasms, unintentional injuries, and COVID‑19.  
- Sex‑specific leading cause percentages for heart disease.  
- No state‑level data for COVID mortality, suicide mortality, or state‑specific leading causes.

**Missing**  
- State‑specific COVID‑19 mortality rates (no mention of threshold 35.5).  
- State‑specific suicide mortality rates (no mention of threshold 18).  
- Explicit statement that heart disease is the leading cause of death in every individual state.
